Rule.name: AbstractClassName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the name of an abstract class matches a regular expression specified in the regex property. If that property is null or empty, then this rule is not applied (i.e., it does nothing). It defaults to null, so this rule must be explicitly configured to be active. This rule ignores interfaces.

Rule.name: AbstractClassWithPublicConstructor
Rule.Description: Checks for abstract classes that define a public constructor, which is useless and confusing.

Rule.name: AbstractClassWithoutAbstractMethod
Rule.Description: The abstract class does not contain any abstract methods. An abstract class suggests an incomplete implementation, which is to be completed by subclasses implementing the abstract methods. If the class is intended to be used as a base class only (not to be instantiated direcly) a protected constructor can be provided prevent direct instantiation.

Rule.name: AddEmptyString
Rule.Description: Finds empty string literals which are being added. This is an inefficient way to convert any type to a String.

Rule.name: AssertWithinFinallyBlock
Rule.Description: Checks for assert statements within a finally block. An assert can throw an exception, hiding the original exception, if there is one.

Rule.name: AssignCollectionSort
Rule.Description: The Collections.sort() method mutates the list and returns the list as a value. If you are assigning the result of sort() to a variable, then you probably don't realize that you're also modifying the original list as well. This is frequently the cause of subtle bugs.

Rule.name: AssignCollectionUnique
Rule.Description: The Collections.unique() method mutates the list and returns the list as a value. If you are assigning the result of unique() to a variable, then you probably don't realize that you're also modifying the original list as well. This is frequently the cause of subtle bugs.

Rule.name: AssignmentInConditional
Rule.Description: An assignment operator (=) was used in a conditional test. This is usually a typo, and the comparison operator (==) was intended.

Rule.name: AssignmentToStaticFieldFromInstanceMethod
Rule.Description: Checks for assignment to a static field from an instance method.

Rule.name: BigDecimalInstantiation
Rule.Description: Checks for calls to the BigDecimal constructors that take a double parameter, which may result in an unexpected BigDecimal value.

Rule.name: BitwiseOperatorInConditional
Rule.Description: Checks for bitwise operations in conditionals, if you need to do a bitwise operation then it is best practice to extract a temp variable.

Rule.name: BlankLineBeforePackage
Rule.Description: Makes sure there are no blank lines before the package declaration of a source code file.

Rule.name: BlockEndsWithBlankLine
Rule.Description: Checks that code blocks such as method bodies, closures and control structure bodies do not end with an empty line.

Rule.name: BlockStartsWithBlankLine
Rule.Description: Checks that code blocks such as method bodies, closures and control structure bodies do not start with an empty line.

Rule.name: BooleanGetBoolean
Rule.Description: This rule catches usages of java.lang.Boolean.getBoolean(String) which reads a boolean from the System properties. It is often mistakenly used to attempt to read user input or parse a String into a boolean. It is a poor piece of API to use; replace it with System.properties['prop'].

Rule.name: BooleanMethodReturnsNull
Rule.Description: Method with Boolean return type returns explicit null. A method that returns either Boolean.TRUE, Boolean.FALSE or null is an accident waiting to happen. This method can be invoked as though it returned a value of type boolean, and the compiler will insert automatic unboxing of the Boolean value. If a null value is returned, this will result in a NullPointerException.

Rule.name: BracesForClass
Rule.Description: Checks the location of the opening brace ({) for classes. By default, requires them on the same line, but the sameLine property can be set to false to override this.

Rule.name: BracesForForLoop
Rule.Description: Checks the location of the opening brace ({) for for loops. By default, requires them on the same line, but the sameLine property can be set to false to override this.

Rule.name: BracesForIfElse
Rule.Description: Checks the location of the opening brace ({) for if statements. By default, requires them on the same line, but the sameLine property can be set to false to override this.

Rule.name: BracesForMethod
Rule.Description: Checks the location of the opening brace ({) for constructors and methods. By default, requires them on the same line, but the sameLine property can be set to false to override this.

Rule.name: BracesForTryCatchFinally
Rule.Description: Checks the location of the opening brace ({) for try statements. By default, requires them on the line, but the sameLine property can be set to false to override this.

Rule.name: BrokenNullCheck
Rule.Description: Looks for faulty checks for null that can cause a NullPointerException.

Rule.name: BrokenOddnessCheck
Rule.Description: The code uses x % 2 == 1 to check to see if a value is odd, but this won't work for negative numbers (e.g., (-5) % 2 == -1). If this code is intending to check for oddness, consider using x & 1 == 1, or x % 2 != 0.

Rule.name: BuilderMethodWithSideEffects
Rule.Description: A builder method is defined as one that creates objects. As such, they should never be of void return type. If a method is named build, create, or make, then it should always return a value.

Rule.name: BusyWait
Rule.Description: Busy waiting (forcing a Thread.sleep() while waiting on a condition) should be avoided. Prefer using the gate and barrier objects in the java.util.concurrent package.

Rule.name: CatchArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
Rule.Description: Check the size of the array before accessing an array element rather than catching ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Rule.name: CatchError
Rule.Description: Catching Error is dangerous; it can catch exceptions such as ThreadDeath and OutOfMemoryError.

Rule.name: CatchException
Rule.Description: Catching Exception is often too broad or general. It should usually be restricted to framework or infrastructure code, rather than application code.

Rule.name: CatchIllegalMonitorStateException
Rule.Description: Dubious catching of IllegalMonitorStateException. IllegalMonitorStateException is generally only thrown in case of a design flaw in your code (calling wait or notify on an object you do not hold a lock on).

Rule.name: CatchIndexOutOfBoundsException
Rule.Description: Check that an index is valid before accessing an indexed element rather than catching IndexOutOfBoundsException.

Rule.name: CatchNullPointerException
Rule.Description: Catching NullPointerException is never appropriate. It should be avoided in the first place with proper null checking, and it can mask underlying errors.

Rule.name: CatchRuntimeException
Rule.Description: Catching RuntimeException is often too broad or general. It should usually be restricted to framework or infrastructure code, rather than application code.

Rule.name: CatchThrowable
Rule.Description: Catching Throwable is dangerous; it can catch exceptions such as ThreadDeath and OutOfMemoryError.

Rule.name: ChainedTest
Rule.Description: A test method that invokes another test method is a chained test; the methods are dependent on one another. Tests should be isolated, and not be dependent on one another.

Rule.name: ClassEndsWithBlankLine
Rule.Description: Check whether the class ends with a blank line.By default, it enforces that there must be a blank line before the closing class brace, except if the class is empty and is written in a single line. A blank line is defined as any line that does not contain any visible characters.

Rule.name: ClassForName
Rule.Description: Using Class.forName(...) is a common way to add dynamic behavior to a system. However, using this method can cause resource leaks because the classes can be pinned in memory for long periods of time.

Rule.name: ClassJavadoc
Rule.Description: Makes sure each class and interface definition is preceded by javadoc. Enum definitions are not checked, due to strange behavior in the Groovy AST.

Rule.name: ClassName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the name of a class matches a regular expression. By default it checks that the class name starts with an uppercase letter and is followed by zero or more word characters (letters, numbers or underscores). The regex property specifies the regular expression used to validate the class name.

Rule.name: ClassNameSameAsFilename
Rule.Description: Reports files containing only one top level class / enum / interface which is named differently than the file.

Rule.name: ClassNameSameAsSuperclass
Rule.Description: Checks for any class that has an identical name to its superclass, other than the package. This can be very confusing.

Rule.name: ClassNotSerializable
Rule.Description: Classes in Jenkins pipeline libraries and Jenkinsfiles should generally implement the Serializable interface because every expression/variable used in a CPS transformed method can potentially be serialized

Rule.name: ClassSize
Rule.Description: Checks if the size of a class exceeds the number of lines specified by the maxLines property (1000).

Rule.name: ClassStartsWithBlankLine
Rule.Description: Check whether the class starts with a blank line. By default, it enforces that there must be a blank line after the opening class brace, except if the class is empty and is written in a single line. A blank line is defined as any line that does not contain any visible characters.

Rule.name: CloneWithoutCloneable
Rule.Description: The method clone() should only be declared if the class implements the Cloneable interface.

Rule.name: CloneableWithoutClone
Rule.Description: A class that implements java.lang.Cloneable should define a clone() method.

Rule.name: CloseWithoutCloseable
Rule.Description: If a class defines a "void close()" then that class should implement java.io.Closeable or java.lang.AutoCloseable.

Rule.name: ClosureAsLastMethodParameter
Rule.Description: If a method is called and the last parameter is an inline closure then it can be declared outside of the method call brackets.

Rule.name: ClosureInGString
Rule.Description: Closures are CPS transformed in Jenkins and will cause an error at runtime when used in GStrings. Typically, they can be replaced by variable interpolation

Rule.name: ClosureStatementOnOpeningLineOfMultipleLineClosure
Rule.Description: Checks for closure logic on first line (after ->) for a multi-line closure.

Rule.name: CollectAllIsDeprecated
Rule.Description: collectAll{} is deprecated since Groovy 1.8.1. Use collectNested instead{}.

Rule.name: CompareToWithoutComparable
Rule.Description: If you implement a compareTo method then you should also implement the Comparable interface.

Rule.name: ComparisonOfTwoConstants
Rule.Description: Checks for expressions where a comparison operator or equals() or compareTo() is used to compare two constants to each other or two literals that contain only constant values, e.g.: 23 == 67, Boolean.FALSE != false, 0.17 <= 0.99, "abc" > "ddd", [a:1] <=> [a:2], [1,2].equals([3,4]) or [a:false, b:true].compareTo(['a':34.5, b:Boolean.TRUE], where x is a variable.

Rule.name: ComparisonWithSelf
Rule.Description: Checks for expressions where a comparison operator or equals() or compareTo() is used to compare a variable to itself, e.g.: x == x, x != x, x <=> x, x < x, x >= x, x.equals(x) or x.compareTo(x), where x is a variable.

Rule.name: CompileStatic
Rule.Description: Check that classes are explicitely annotated with either @GrailsCompileStatic, @CompileStatic or @CompileDynamic

Rule.name: ConfusingClassNamedException
Rule.Description: This class is not derived from another exception, but ends with 'Exception'. This will be confusing to users of this class.

Rule.name: ConfusingMethodName
Rule.Description: Checks for confusing method names. The referenced methods have names that differ only by capitalization. This is very confusing because if the capitalization were identical then one of the methods would override the other.

Rule.name: ConfusingMultipleReturns
Rule.Description: Multiple return values can be used to set several variables at once. To use multiple return values, the left hand side of the assignment must be enclosed in parenthesis. If not, then you are not using multiple return values, you're only assigning the last element.

Rule.name: ConfusingTernary
Rule.Description: In a ternary expression avoid negation in the test. For example, rephrase: "(x != y) ? diff : same" as: "(x == y) ? same : diff". Consistent use of this rule makes the code easier to read. Also, this resolves trivial ordering problems, such as "does the error case go first?" or "does the common case go first?".

Rule.name: ConsecutiveBlankLines
Rule.Description: Makes sure there are no consecutive lines that are either blank or whitespace only.

Rule.name: ConsecutiveLiteralAppends
Rule.Description: Violations occur when method calls to append(Object) are chained together with literals as parameters. The chained calls can be joined into one invocation.

Rule.name: ConsecutiveStringConcatenation
Rule.Description: Catches concatenation of two string literals on the same line. These can safely by joined.

Rule.name: ConstantAssertExpression
Rule.Description: Checks for assert statements where the assert boolean condition expression is a constant or literal value.

Rule.name: ConstantIfExpression
Rule.Description: Checks for if statements with a constant value for the if expression, such as true, false, null, or a literal constant value.

Rule.name: ConstantTernaryExpression
Rule.Description: Checks for ternary expressions with a constant value for the boolean expression, such as true, false, null, or a literal constant value.

Rule.name: ConstantsOnlyInterface
Rule.Description: An interface should be used only to model a behaviour of a class: using an interface as a container of constants is a poor usage pattern.

Rule.name: CouldBeElvis
Rule.Description: Catch an if block that could be written as an elvis expression.

Rule.name: CouldBeSwitchStatement
Rule.Description: Checks for multiple if statements that could be converted to a switch

Rule.name: CoupledTestCase
Rule.Description: This rule finds test cases that are coupled to other test cases, either by invoking static methods on another test case or by creating instances of another test case. If you require shared logic in test cases then extract that logic to a new class where it can properly be reused.

Rule.name: CpsCallFromNonCpsMethod
Rule.Description: CPS transformed methods may not be called from non CPS transformed methods in Jenkins

Rule.name: CrapMetric
Rule.Description: Checks the CRAP (Change Risk Anti-Patterns) score for methods/classes. The CRAP metric score is based on the cyclomatic complexity and test coverage for individual methods. A method with a CRAP value greater than the maxMethodCrapScore property (30) causes a violation. Likewise, a class that has an (average method) CRAP value greater than the maxClassAverageMethodCrapScore property (30) causes a violation.

Rule.name: CyclomaticComplexity
Rule.Description: Checks the cyclomatic complexity for methods/classes.A method (or "closure field") with a cyclomatic complexity value greater than the maxMethodComplexity property (20) causes a violation. Likewise, a class that has an (average method) cyclomatic complexityvalue greater than the maxClassAverageMethodComplexity property (20) causes a violation.

Rule.name: DeadCode
Rule.Description: Dead code appears after a return statement or an exception is thrown. If code appears after one of these statements then it will never be executed and can be safely deleted.

Rule.name: DirectConnectionManagement
Rule.Description: The J2EE standard requires that applications use the container's resource management facilities to obtain connections to resources. Every major web application container provides pooled database connection management as part of its resource management framework. Duplicating this functionality in an application is difficult and error prone, which is part of the reason it is forbidden under the J2EE standard.

Rule.name: DoubleCheckedLocking
Rule.Description: This rule detects double checked locking, where a 'lock hint' is tested for null before initializing an object within a synchronized block. Double checked locking does not guarantee correctness and is an anti-pattern.

Rule.name: DoubleNegative
Rule.Description: There is no point in using a double negative, it is always positive. For instance !!x can always be simplified to x. And !(!x) can as well.

Rule.name: DuplicateCaseStatement
Rule.Description: Check for duplicate case statements in a switch block, such as two equal integers or strings.

Rule.name: DuplicateImport
Rule.Description: Duplicate import statements are unnecessary.

Rule.name: DuplicateListLiteral
Rule.Description: Code containing duplicate List literals can usually be improved by declaring the List as a constant field.

Rule.name: DuplicateMapKey
Rule.Description: A map literal is created with duplicated key. The map entry will be overwritten.

Rule.name: DuplicateMapLiteral
Rule.Description: Code containing duplicate Map literals can usually be improved by declaring the Map as a constant field.

Rule.name: DuplicateNumberLiteral
Rule.Description: Code containing duplicate number literals can usually be improved by declaring the number as a constant field. The ignoreNumbers property (0,1) can optionally specify a comma-separated list of numbers to ignore.

Rule.name: DuplicateSetValue
Rule.Description: A Set literal is created with duplicate constant value. A set cannot contain two elements with the same value.

Rule.name: DuplicateStringLiteral
Rule.Description: Code containing duplicate String literals can usually be improved by declaring the String as a constant field. The ignoreStrings property () can optionally specify a comma-separated list of Strings to ignore.

Rule.name: ElseBlockBraces
Rule.Description: Use braces for else blocks, even for a single statement. By default, braces are not required for an else if it is followed immediately by an if. Set the bracesRequiredForElseIf property to true to require braces is that situation as well.

Rule.name: EmptyCatchBlock
Rule.Description: In most cases, exceptions should not be caught and ignored (swallowed).

Rule.name: EmptyClass
Rule.Description: Reports classes without methods, fields or properties. Why would you need a class like this?

Rule.name: EmptyElseBlock
Rule.Description: Empty else blocks are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EmptyFinallyBlock
Rule.Description: Empty finally blocks are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EmptyForStatement
Rule.Description: Empty for statements are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EmptyIfStatement
Rule.Description: Empty if statements are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EmptyInstanceInitializer
Rule.Description: An empty class instance initializer was found. It is safe to remove it.

Rule.name: EmptyMethod
Rule.Description: A method was found without an implementation. If the method is overriding or implementing a parent method, then mark it with the @Override annotation.

Rule.name: EmptyMethodInAbstractClass
Rule.Description: An empty method in an abstract class should be abstract instead, as developer may rely on this empty implementation rather than code the appropriate one.

Rule.name: EmptyStaticInitializer
Rule.Description: An empty static initializer was found. It is safe to remove it.

Rule.name: EmptySwitchStatement
Rule.Description: Empty switch statements are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EmptySynchronizedStatement
Rule.Description: Empty synchronized statements are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EmptyTryBlock
Rule.Description: Empty try blocks are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EmptyWhileStatement
Rule.Description: Empty while statements are confusing and serve no purpose.

Rule.name: EnumCustomSerializationIgnored
Rule.Description: Checks for enums that define writeObject() or writeReplace() methods, or declare serialPersistentFields or serialVersionUID fields, all of which are ignored for enums.

Rule.name: EqualsAndHashCode
Rule.Description: If either the equals(Object) or the hashCode() methods are overridden within a class, then both must be overridden.

Rule.name: EqualsOverloaded
Rule.Description: The class has an equals method, but the parameter of the method is not of type Object. It is not overriding equals but instead overloading it.

Rule.name: ExceptionExtendsError
Rule.Description: Errors are system exceptions. Do not extend them.

Rule.name: ExceptionExtendsThrowable
Rule.Description: Checks for classes that extend Throwable. Custom exception classes should subclass Exception or one of its descendants.

Rule.name: ExceptionNotThrown
Rule.Description: Checks for an exception constructor call without a throw as the last statement within a catch block.

Rule.name: ExplicitArrayListInstantiation
Rule.Description: This rule checks for the explicit instantiation of a ArrayList using the no-arg constructor. In Groovy, it is best to write "new ArrayList()" as "[]", which creates the same object.

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToAndMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the and(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the & operator. A groovier way to express this: a.and(b) is this: a & b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToCompareToMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the compareTo(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the <=>, >, >=, <, and <= operators. A groovier way to express this: a.compareTo(b) is this: a <=> b, or using the other operators.

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToDivMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the div(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the / operator. A groovier way to express this: a.div(b) is this: a / b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToEqualsMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the equals(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the == or != operator. A groovier way to express this: a.equals(b) is this: a == b and a groovier way to express : !a.equals(b) is : a != b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToGetAtMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the getAt(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the [] index operator. A groovier way to express this: a.getAt(b) is this: a[b]

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToLeftShiftMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the leftShift(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the << operator. A groovier way to express this: a.leftShift(b) is this: a << b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToMinusMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the minus(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the - operator. A groovier way to express this: a.minus(b) is this: a - b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToModMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the mod(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the % operator. A groovier way to express this: a.mod(b) is this: a % b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToMultiplyMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the minus(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the * operator. A groovier way to express this: a.multiply(b) is this: a * b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToOrMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the or(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the | operator. A groovier way to express this: a.or(b) is this: a | b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToPlusMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the plus(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the + operator. A groovier way to express this: a.plus(b) is this: a + b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToPowerMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the power(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the ** operator. A groovier way to express this: a.power(b) is this: a ** b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToPutAtMethod
Rule.Description: Detects when the putAt(Object, Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the [] index operator. A groovier way to express this: map.putAt(k, v) is this: map[k] = v.

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToRightShiftMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the rightShift(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the >> operator. A groovier way to express this: a.rightShift(b) is this: a >> b

Rule.name: ExplicitCallToXorMethod
Rule.Description: This rule detects when the xor(Object) method is called directly in code instead of using the ^ operator. A groovier way to express this: a.xor(b) is this: a ^ b

Rule.name: ExplicitGarbageCollection
Rule.Description: Calls to System.gc(), Runtime.getRuntime().gc(), and System.runFinalization() are not advised. Code should have the same behavior whether the garbage collection is disabled using the option -Xdisableexplicitgc or not. Moreover, "modern" jvms do a very good job handling garbage collections. If memory usage issues unrelated to memory leaks develop within an application, it should be dealt with JVM options rather than within the code itself.

Rule.name: ExplicitHashMapInstantiation
Rule.Description: This rule checks for the explicit instantiation of a HashMap using the no-arg constructor. In Groovy, it is best to write "new HashMap()" as "[:]", which creates the same object.

Rule.name: ExplicitHashSetInstantiation
Rule.Description: This rule checks for the explicit instantiation of a HashSet using the no-arg constructor. In Groovy, it is best to write "new HashSet()" as "[] as Set", which creates the same object.

Rule.name: ExplicitLinkedHashMapInstantiation
Rule.Description: This rule checks for the explicit instantiation of a LinkedHashMap using the no-arg constructor. In Groovy, it is best to write "new LinkedHashMap()" as "[:]", which creates the same object.

Rule.name: ExplicitLinkedListInstantiation
Rule.Description: This rule checks for the explicit instantiation of a LinkedList using the no-arg constructor. In Groovy, it is best to write "new LinkedList()" as "[] as Queue", which creates the same object.

Rule.name: ExplicitStackInstantiation
Rule.Description: This rule checks for the explicit instantiation of a Stack using the no-arg constructor. In Groovy, it is best to write "new Stack()" as "[] as Stack", which creates the same object.

Rule.name: ExplicitTreeSetInstantiation
Rule.Description: This rule checks for the explicit instantiation of a TreeSet using the no-arg constructor. In Groovy, it is best to write "new TreeSet()" as "[] as SortedSet", which creates the same object.

Rule.name: ExpressionInCpsMethodNotSerializable
Rule.Description: Every expression/variable in a CPS transformed method in Jenkins can potentially be serialized and should therefore implement the Serializable interface

Rule.name: FactoryMethodName
Rule.Description: A factory method is a method that creates objects, and they are typically named either buildFoo(), makeFoo(), or createFoo(). This rule enforces that only one naming convention is used. It defaults to makeFoo(), but that can be changed using the property 'regex'.

Rule.name: FieldName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the name of each field matches a regular expression. By default it checks that non-'final' field names start with a lowercase letter and contains only letters or numbers, and 'final' field names start with an uppercase letter and contain only uppercase letters, numbers and underscores. The regex property specifies the default regular expression used to validate field names. The finalRegex property specifies the regular expression to validate 'final' field names. The staticRegex property specifies the regular expression to validate 'static' field names. The staticFinalRegex property specifies the regular expression to validate 'static final' field names. The ignoreFieldNames property (serialVersionUID) can specify field names that should be ignored, optionally containing wildcard characters ('*' or '?').

Rule.name: FieldTypeRequired
Rule.Description: Checks that field types are explicitly specified (and not using def).

Rule.name: FileCreateTempFile
Rule.Description: The File.createTempFile() method is insecure, and has been deprecated by the ESAPI secure coding library. It has been replaced by the ESAPI Randomizer.getRandomFilename(String) method.

Rule.name: FileEndsWithoutNewline
Rule.Description: Makes sure the source code file ends with a newline character.

Rule.name: FinalClassWithProtectedMember
Rule.Description: This rule finds classes marked final that contain protected methods. If a class is final then it may not be subclassed, and there is therefore no point in having a method with protected visibility. Either the class should not be final or the method should be private or protected.

Rule.name: ForLoopShouldBeWhileLoop
Rule.Description: A for loop without an init and update statement can be simplified to a while loop.

Rule.name: ForStatementBraces
Rule.Description: Use braces for for statements, even for a single statement.

Rule.name: ForbiddenCallInCpsMethod
Rule.Description: Some methods from the standard library cannot be CPS transformed and therefore must not be called from CPS transformed methods in Jenkins

Rule.name: GStringAsMapKey
Rule.Description: A GString should not be used as a map key since its hashcode is not guaranteed to be stable. Consider calling key.toString().

Rule.name: GStringExpressionWithinString
Rule.Description: Check for regular (single quote) strings containing a GString-type expression (${...}).

Rule.name: GetterMethodCouldBeProperty
Rule.Description: If a class defines a public method that follows the Java getter notation, and returns a constant, then it is cleaner to provide a Groovy property for the value rather than a Groovy method.

Rule.name: GrailsDomainGormMethods
Rule.Description: Database operation should be performed by Data Services instead of calling GORM static or instance methods.

Rule.name: GrailsDomainHasEquals
Rule.Description: Checks that Grails domain classes redefine equals().

Rule.name: GrailsDomainHasToString
Rule.Description: Checks that Grails domain classes redefine toString()

Rule.name: GrailsDomainReservedSqlKeywordName
Rule.Description: Forbids usage of SQL reserved keywords as class or field names in Grails domain classes. Naming a domain class (or its field) with such a keyword causes SQL schema creation errors and/or redundant table/column name mappings.

Rule.name: GrailsDomainStringPropertyMaxSize
Rule.Description: String properties in Grails domain classes have to define maximum size otherwise the property is mapped to VARCHAR(255) causing runtime exceptions to occur

Rule.name: GrailsDomainWithServiceReference
Rule.Description: Checks that Grails domain classes do not have service classes injected.

Rule.name: GrailsDuplicateConstraint
Rule.Description: Check for duplicate entry in domain class constraints

Rule.name: GrailsDuplicateMapping
Rule.Description: Check for duplicate name in a domain class mapping

Rule.name: GrailsMassAssignment
Rule.Description: Untrusted input should not be allowed to set arbitrary object fields without restriction.

Rule.name: GrailsServletContextReference
Rule.Description: Checks for references to the servletContext object from within Grails controller and taglib classes.

Rule.name: GrailsStatelessService
Rule.Description: Checks for fields on Grails service classes. Grails service classes are singletons, by default, and so they should be reentrant and typically stateless. The ignoreFieldNames property (dataSource,scope,sessionFactory,transactional,*Service,grailsApplication) specifies one or more field names that should be ignored. The ignoreFieldTypes property (null) specifies one or more field type names that should be ignored. Both can optionally contain wildcard characters ('*' or '?').

Rule.name: GroovyLangImmutable
Rule.Description: The groovy.lang.Immutable annotation has been deprecated and replaced by groovy.transform.Immutable. Do not use the Immutable in groovy.lang.

Rule.name: HardCodedWindowsFileSeparator
Rule.Description: This rule finds usages of a Windows file separator within the constructor call of a File object. It is better to use the Unix file separator or use the File.separator constant.

Rule.name: HardCodedWindowsRootDirectory
Rule.Description: This rule find cases where a File object is constructed with a windows-based path. This is not portable, and using the File.listRoots() method is a better alternative.

Rule.name: HashtableIsObsolete
Rule.Description: The java.util.Hashtable class is effectively obsolete. Use the Java Collections Framework classes instead, including HashMap or ConcurrentHashMap. See the JDK javadoc.

Rule.name: IfStatementBraces
Rule.Description: Use braces for if statements, even for a single statement.

Rule.name: IfStatementCouldBeTernary
Rule.Description: Checks for if statements where both the if and else blocks contain only a single return statement with a constant or literal value

Rule.name: IllegalClassMember
Rule.Description: Checks for classes containing fields/properties/methods matching configured illegal member modifiers or not matching any of the configured allowed member modifiers.

Rule.name: IllegalClassReference
Rule.Description: Checks for reference to any of the classes configured in classNames.

Rule.name: IllegalPackageReference
Rule.Description: Checks for reference to any of the packages configured in packageNames.

Rule.name: IllegalRegex
Rule.Description: Checks for a specified illegal regular expression within the source code. The regex property specifies the regular expression to check for. It is required and cannot be null or empty.

Rule.name: IllegalString
Rule.Description: Checks for a specified illegal string within the source code.

Rule.name: IllegalSubclass
Rule.Description: Checks for classes that extend one of the specified set of illegal superclasses configured in superclassNames.

Rule.name: ImplementationAsType
Rule.Description: Checks for use of a predefined set of concrete classes (e.g. ArrayList, Hashtable, ConcurrentHashMap) when specifying the type of a method parameter, closure parameter, constructor parameter, method return type or field type. The associated interfaces should be used to specify the type instead.

Rule.name: ImplicitClosureParameter
Rule.Description: Checks that the implicit it closure parameter is not used and that parameters are declared explicitly instead.

Rule.name: ImplicitReturnStatement
Rule.Description: Check for a non-void method that is missing an explicit return statement.

Rule.name: ImportFromSamePackage
Rule.Description: An import of a class that is within the same package is unnecessary.

Rule.name: ImportFromSunPackages
Rule.Description: Avoid importing anything from the 'sun.*' packages. These packages are not portable and are likely to change.

Rule.name: InconsistentPropertyLocking
Rule.Description: Class contains similarly-named get and set methods where one method of the pair is marked either @WithReadLock or @WithWriteLock and the other is not locked at all.

Rule.name: InconsistentPropertySynchronization
Rule.Description: Class contains similarly-named get and set methods where the set method is synchronized and the get method is not, or the get method is synchronized and the set method is not.

Rule.name: Indentation
Rule.Description: Check indentation for class and method declarations, and initial statements.

Rule.name: InsecureRandom
Rule.Description: Reports usages of java.util.Random, which can produce very predictable results. If two instances of Random are created with the same seed and sequence of method calls, they will generate the exact same results. Use java.security.SecureRandom instead, which provides a cryptographically strong random number generator. SecureRandom uses PRNG, which means they are using a deterministic algorithm to produce a pseudo-random number from a true random seed. SecureRandom produces non-deterministic output.

Rule.name: Instanceof
Rule.Description: Checks for use of the instanceof operator. Use the ignoreTypeNames property to configure ignored type names.

Rule.name: IntegerGetInteger
Rule.Description: This rule catches usages of java.lang.Integer.getInteger(String, ...) which reads an Integer from the System properties. It is often mistakenly used to attempt to read user input or parse a String into an Integer. It is a poor piece of API to use; replace it with System.properties['prop'].

Rule.name: InterfaceName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the name of an interface matches a regular expression specified in the regex property. If that property is null or empty, then this rule is not applied (i.e., it does nothing). It defaults to null, so this rule must be explicitly configured to be active.

Rule.name: InterfaceNameSameAsSuperInterface
Rule.Description: Checks for any interface that has an identical name to its super-interface, other than the package. This can be very confusing.

Rule.name: InvertedCondition
Rule.Description: An inverted condition is one where a constant expression is used on the left hand side of the equals comparision. Such conditions can be confusing especially when used in assertions where the expected value is by convention placed on the right hand side of the comparision.

Rule.name: InvertedIfElse
Rule.Description: An inverted if-else statement is one in which there is a single if statement with a single else branch and the boolean test of the if is negated. For instance "if (!x) false else true". It is usually clearer to write this as "if (x) true else false".

Rule.name: JUnitAssertAlwaysFails
Rule.Description: Checks for JUnit assert() method calls with constant arguments such that the assertion always fails. This includes: assertTrue(false), assertFalse(true) and assertNull(CONSTANT).

Rule.name: JUnitAssertAlwaysSucceeds
Rule.Description: Checks for JUnit assert() method calls with constant arguments such that the assertion always succeeds. This includes: assertTrue(true), assertFalse(false) and assertNull(null).

Rule.name: JUnitAssertEqualsConstantActualValue
Rule.Description: Reports usages of org.junit.Assert.assertEquals([message,] expected, actual) where the 'actual' parameter is a constant or a literal. Most likely it was intended to be the 'expected' value.

Rule.name: JUnitFailWithoutMessage
Rule.Description: This rule detects JUnit calling the fail() method without an argument. For better error reporting you should always provide a message.

Rule.name: JUnitLostTest
Rule.Description: Checks for classes that import JUnit 4 classes and contain a public, instance, void, no-arg method named test* that is not annotated with @Test.

Rule.name: JUnitPublicField
Rule.Description: Checks for public field on a JUnit test class

Rule.name: JUnitPublicNonTestMethod
Rule.Description: Checks if a JUnit test class contains public methods other than standard test methods, JUnit framework methods or methods with JUnit annotations.

Rule.name: JUnitPublicProperty
Rule.Description: Checks for public properties defined on JUnit test classes. There should be no need to expose a public property on a test class.

Rule.name: JUnitSetUpCallsSuper
Rule.Description: Checks that if the JUnit setUp() method is defined, that it includes a call to super.setUp().

Rule.name: JUnitStyleAssertions
Rule.Description: This rule detects calling JUnit style assertions like assertEquals, assertTrue, assertFalse, assertNull, assertNotNull. Groovy ships with a feature called the "power assert", which is an assert statement with better error reporting. This is preferable to the JUnit assertions.

Rule.name: JUnitTearDownCallsSuper
Rule.Description: Checks that if the JUnit tearDown() method is defined, that it includes a call to super.tearDown().

Rule.name: JUnitTestMethodWithoutAssert
Rule.Description: This rule searches for test methods that do not contain assert statements. Either the test method is missing assert statements, which is an error, or the test method contains custom assert statements that do not follow a proper assert naming convention. Test methods are defined as public void methods that begin with the work test or have a @Test annotation. By default this rule applies to the default test class names, but this can be changed using the rule's applyToClassNames property.

Rule.name: JUnitUnnecessarySetUp
Rule.Description: Checks for JUnit setUp() methods that contain only a call to super.setUp().

Rule.name: JUnitUnnecessaryTearDown
Rule.Description: Checks for JUnit tearDown() methods that contain only a call to super.tearDown().

Rule.name: JUnitUnnecessaryThrowsException
Rule.Description: Check for throws clauses on JUnit test methods. That is not necessary in Groovy.

Rule.name: JavaIoPackageAccess
Rule.Description: This rule reports violations of the Enterprise JavaBeans specification by using the java.io package to access files or the file system.

Rule.name: JavadocConsecutiveEmptyLines
Rule.Description: Checks for javadoc comments with more than one consecutive empty line.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyAuthorTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @author tags within javadoc.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyExceptionTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @exception tag within javadoc.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyFirstLine
Rule.Description: Check for javadoc comments with an empty top line.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyLastLine
Rule.Description: Check for javadoc comments with an empty line at the bottom.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyParamTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @param tags within javadoc.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyReturnTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @return tags within javadoc.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptySeeTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @see tags within javadoc.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptySinceTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @since tags within javadoc.

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyThrowsTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @throws tag within javadoc

Rule.name: JavadocEmptyVersionTag
Rule.Description: Checks for empty @version tags within javadoc.

Rule.name: JavadocMissingExceptionDescription
Rule.Description: Checks for missing description within @exception javadoc tags.

Rule.name: JavadocMissingParamDescription
Rule.Description: Checks for missing description within @param javadoc tags.

Rule.name: JavadocMissingThrowsDescription
Rule.Description: Checks for missing description within @throws javadoc tags.

Rule.name: JdbcConnectionReference
Rule.Description: Check for direct use of java.sql.Connection, which is discouraged and almost never necessary in application code.

Rule.name: JdbcResultSetReference
Rule.Description: Check for direct use of java.sql.ResultSet, which is not necessary if using the Groovy Sql facility or an ORM framework such as Hibernate.

Rule.name: JdbcStatementReference
Rule.Description: Check for direct use of java.sql.Statement, java.sql.PreparedStatement, or java.sql.CallableStatement, which is not necessary if using the Groovy Sql facility or an ORM framework such as Hibernate.

Rule.name: LineLength
Rule.Description: Checks the maximum length for each line of source code. It checks for number of characters, so lines that include tabs may appear longer than the allowed number when viewing the file. The maximum line length can be configured by setting the length property, which defaults to 120.

Rule.name: LocaleSetDefault
Rule.Description: Checks for calls to Locale.setDefault(), which sets the Locale across the entire JVM.

Rule.name: LoggerForDifferentClass
Rule.Description: Checks for instantiating a logger (Log4J, SLF4J, Logback, Apache Commons Logging or Java Util Logging) for a class other than the current class.

Rule.name: LoggerWithWrongModifiers
Rule.Description: Logger objects should be declared private, static and final. If subclasses should have access to a Logger in a parent class then the Logger should be declared protected, non-static and final. This rule find loggers that are not declared with these modifiers.

Rule.name: LoggingSwallowsStacktrace
Rule.Description: If you are logging an exception then the proper API is to call error(Object, Throwable), which will log the message and the exception stack trace. If you call error(Object) then the stacktrace may not be logged.

Rule.name: LongLiteralWithLowerCaseL
Rule.Description: In Java and Groovy, you can specify long literals with the L or l character, for instance 55L or 24l. It is best practice to always use an uppercase L and never a lowercase l. This is because 11l rendered in some fonts may look like 111 instead of 11L.

Rule.name: MethodCount
Rule.Description: A class with too many methods is probably a good suspect for refactoring, in order to reduce its complexity and find a way to have more fine grained objects. The <em>maxMethods</em> property (30) specifies the threshold.

Rule.name: MethodName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the name of each method matches a regular expression. By default it checks that the method name starts with a lowercase letter. The regex property specifies the regular expression to check the method name against. The ignoreMethodNames property (null) can specify method names that should be ignored, optionally containing wildcard characters ('*' or '?').

Rule.name: MethodParameterTypeRequired
Rule.Description: Checks that method parameters are not dynamically typed, that is they are explicitly stated and different than def.

Rule.name: MethodReturnTypeRequired
Rule.Description: Checks that method return types are not dynamic, that is they are explicitly stated and different than def.

Rule.name: MethodSize
Rule.Description: Checks if the size of a method exceeds the number of lines specified by the maxLines property (100).

Rule.name: MisorderedStaticImports
Rule.Description: Static imports should never be declared after nonstatic imports.

Rule.name: MissingBlankLineAfterImports
Rule.Description: Makes sure there is a blank line after the imports of a source code file.

Rule.name: MissingBlankLineAfterPackage
Rule.Description: Makes sure there is a blank line after the package statement of a source code file.

Rule.name: MissingBlankLineBeforeAnnotatedField
Rule.Description: Checks that there is a blank line before a field declaration that uses annotations.

Rule.name: MissingNewInThrowStatement
Rule.Description: A common Groovy mistake when throwing exceptions is to forget the new keyword. For instance, "throw RuntimeException()" instead of "throw new RuntimeException()". If the error path is not unit tested then the production system will throw a Method Missing exception and hide the root cause. This rule finds constructs like "throw RuntimeException()" that look like a new keyword was meant to be used but forgotten.

Rule.name: MissingOverrideAnnotation
Rule.Description: Checks for methods that override a method in a super class or implement a method in an interface but are not annotated with @Override.

Rule.name: MultipleLoggers
Rule.Description: This rule catches classes that have more than one logger object defined. Typically, a class has zero or one logger objects.

Rule.name: MultipleUnaryOperators
Rule.Description: Checks for multiple consecutive unary operators. These are confusing, and are likely typos and bugs.

Rule.name: NestedBlockDepth
Rule.Description: Checks for blocks or closures nested more than maxNestedBlockDepth (5) levels deep.

Rule.name: NestedForLoop
Rule.Description: Reports classes with nested for loops.

Rule.name: NestedSynchronization
Rule.Description: Nested synchronized statements should be avoided. Nested synchronized statements are either useless (if the lock objects are identical) or prone to deadlock.

Rule.name: NoDef
Rule.Description: def should not be used. You should replace it with concrete type.

Rule.name: NoDouble
Rule.Description: Checks for use of the double or Double types, in fields, variables, method parameters and method return types.

Rule.name: NoFloat
Rule.Description: Checks for use of the float or Float types, in fields, variables, method parameters and method return types.

Rule.name: NoJavaUtilDate
Rule.Description: Do not use java.util.Date. Prefer the classes in the java.time.* packages.

Rule.name: NoScriptBindings
Rule.Description: Do not use script bindings (global variables). Prefer to scope them as local variables or fields by providing a type definition (int a ...).

Rule.name: NoTabCharacter
Rule.Description: Checks that all source files do not contain the tab character

Rule.name: NoWildcardImports
Rule.Description: Wildcard imports, static or otherwise, should not be used.

Rule.name: NonFinalPublicField
Rule.Description: Finds code that violates secure coding principles for mobile code by declaring a member variable public but not final.

Rule.name: NonFinalSubclassOfSensitiveInterface
Rule.Description: The permissions classes such as java.security.Permission and java.security.BasicPermission are designed to be extended. Classes that derive from these permissions classes, however, must prohibit extension. This prohibition ensures that malicious subclasses cannot change the properties of the derived class. Classes that implement sensitive interfaces such as java.security.PrivilegedAction and java.security.PrivilegedActionException must also be declared final for analogous reasons.

Rule.name: NonSerializableFieldInSerializableClass
Rule.Description: All fields of a class that implements Serializable should also implement it

Rule.name: ObjectFinalize
Rule.Description: The finalize() method should only be called by the JVM after the object has been garbage collected.

Rule.name: ObjectOverrideMisspelledMethodName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the names of the most commonly overridden methods of Object: equals, hashCode and toString, are correct.

Rule.name: ObjectOverrideOnlyNonCpsMethods
Rule.Description: Overridden methods of the standard library (e.g. from java.lang.Object) are often called from there and therefore must not be CPS transformed in Jenkins

Rule.name: OptionalCollectionReturnType
Rule.Description: Do not declare a method return type of Optional<List> (or Collection, ArrayList, Set, Map, HashMap, etc.). Return an empty collection instead.

Rule.name: OptionalField
Rule.Description: Do not use an Optional as a field type.

Rule.name: OptionalMethodParameter
Rule.Description: Do not use an Optional as a parameter type for a method or constructor.

Rule.name: PackageName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the package name for a class matches a regular expression. By default it checks that the package name consists of only lowercase letters, separated by periods. The regex property specifies the regular expression used to validate the package name. The packageNameRequired property indicates whether a package name declaration is required for all classes.

Rule.name: PackageNameMatchesFilePath
Rule.Description: A package source file's path should match the package itself. To find the package-relevant subpath in the file path the groupId needs to be configured. It is expected in every package declaration.

Rule.name: ParameterAssignmentInFilterClosure
Rule.Description: An assignment operator was used on a parameter in a filtering closure. This is usually a typo, and the comparison operator (==) was intended.

Rule.name: ParameterCount
Rule.Description: Checks if the number of parameters in method/constructor exceeds the number of parameters specified by the maxParameters property.

Rule.name: ParameterName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the name of each parameter matches a regular expression. This rule applies to method parameters, constructor parameters and closure parameters. By default it checks that parameter names start with a lowercase letter and contains only letters or numbers. The regex property specifies the default regular expression used to validate the parameter name. The ignoreParameterNames property (null) can specify parameter names that should be ignored, optionally containing wildcard characters ('*' or '?').

Rule.name: ParameterOrReturnTypeNotSerializable
Rule.Description: Every parameter and return type has to implement the Serializable interface in Jenkins

Rule.name: ParameterReassignment
Rule.Description: Checks for a method or closure parameter being reassigned to a new value within the body of the method/closure, which is a confusing and questionable practice. Use a temporary variable instead.

Rule.name: PrintStackTrace
Rule.Description: Checks for calls to printStackTrace().

Rule.name: Println
Rule.Description: Checks for calls to this.print(), this.println() or this.printf().

Rule.name: PrivateFieldCouldBeFinal
Rule.Description: Checks for private fields that are only set within a constructor or field initializer. Such fields can safely be made final.

Rule.name: PropertyName
Rule.Description: Verifies that the name of each property matches a regular expression. By default it checks that property names other than 'static final' start with a lowercase letter and contains only letters or numbers, and 'static final' property names start with an uppercase letter and contain only uppercase letters, numbers and underscores. The regex property specifies the default regular expression used to validate property names. The finalRegex property specifies the regular expression to validate 'final' property names. The staticRegex property specifies the regular expression to validate 'static' property names. The staticFinalRegex property specifies the regular expression to validate 'static final' property names. The ignorePropertyNames property (null) can specify property names that should be ignored, optionally containing wildcard characters ('*' or '?').

Rule.name: PublicFinalizeMethod
Rule.Description: Creates a violation when the program violates secure coding principles by declaring a finalize() method public.

Rule.name: PublicInstanceField
Rule.Description: Using public fields is considered to be a bad design. Use properties instead.

Rule.name: PublicMethodsBeforeNonPublicMethods
Rule.Description: Enforce that all public methods are above protected and private methods.

Rule.name: RandomDoubleCoercedToZero
Rule.Description: The Math.random() method returns a double result greater than or equal to 0.0 and less than 1.0. If you coerce this result into an Integer or int, then it is coerced to zero. Casting the result to int, or assigning it to an int field is probably a bug.

Rule.name: RemoveAllOnSelf
Rule.Description: Don't use removeAll to clear a collection. If you want to remove all elements from a collection c, use c.clear, not c.removeAll(c). Calling c.removeAll(c) to clear a collection is less clear, susceptible to errors from typos, less efficient and for some collections, might throw a ConcurrentModificationException.

Rule.name: RequiredRegex
Rule.Description: Checks for a specified regular expression that must exist within the source code. The regex property specifies the regular expression to check for. It is required and cannot be null or empty.

Rule.name: RequiredString
Rule.Description: Checks for a specified text string that must exist within the source code. The string property specifies the String to check for. It is required and cannot be null or empty.

Rule.name: ReturnFromFinallyBlock
Rule.Description: Returning from a finally block is confusing and can hide the original exception.

Rule.name: ReturnNullFromCatchBlock
Rule.Description: Returning null from a catch block often masks errors and requires the client to handle error codes. In some coding styles this is discouraged.

Rule.name: ReturnsNullInsteadOfEmptyArray
Rule.Description: Consider returning a zero length array rather than null. It is often a better design to return a length zero array rather than a null reference to indicate that there are no results (i.e., an empty list of results). This way, no explicit check for null is needed by clients of the method.

Rule.name: ReturnsNullInsteadOfEmptyCollection
Rule.Description: Consider returning a zero length collection rather than null. It is often a better design to return a length zero collection rather than a null reference to indicate that there are no results (i.e., an empty list of results). This way, no explicit check for null is needed by clients of the method.

Rule.name: SerialPersistentFields
Rule.Description: To use a Serializable object's serialPersistentFields correctly, it must be declared private, static, and final.

Rule.name: SerialVersionUID
Rule.Description: A serialVersionUID is normally intended to be used with Serialization. It needs to be of type long, static, and final. Also, it should have a visibility modifier such as public or private. Providing no modifier creates a Property and Groovy generates a getter, which is probably not intended.

Rule.name: SerializableClassMustDefineSerialVersionUID
Rule.Description: Classes that implement Serializable should define a serialVersionUID. If you don't define serialVersionUID, the system will make one by hashing most of your class's features. Then if you change anything, the UID will change and Java won't let you reload old data.

Rule.name: SimpleDateFormatMissingLocale
Rule.Description: Be sure to specify a Locale when creating a new instance of SimpleDateFormat; the class is locale-sensitive. If you instantiate SimpleDateFormat without a Locale parameter, it will format the date and time according to the default Locale. Both the pattern and the Locale determine the format. For the same pattern, SimpleDateFormat may format a date and time differently if the Locale varies.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterCatch
Rule.Description: Check that there is exactly one space (blank) after the catch keyword and before the opening parenthesis.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterClosingBrace
Rule.Description: Check that there is at least one space (blank) or whitespace after each closing brace ("}") for method/class/interface declarations, closure expressions and block statements.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterComma
Rule.Description: Checks that there is at least one space or whitespace following each comma. That includes checks for method and closure declaration parameter lists, method call parameter lists, Map literals and List literals.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterCommentDelimiter
Rule.Description: Checks that there is whitespace after comment characters (// and /*)

Rule.name: SpaceAfterFor
Rule.Description: Check that there is exactly one space (blank) after the for keyword and before the opening parenthesis.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterIf
Rule.Description: Check that there is exactly one space (blank) after the if keyword and before the opening parenthesis.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterMethodCallName
Rule.Description: Checks that there is whitespace after the method name when a method call contains parenthesis or that there is at most one space after the method name if the call does not contain parenthesis.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterMethodDeclarationName
Rule.Description: Check whether method declarations do not contain unnecessary whitespace between method name and the opening parenthesis for parameter list.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterNotOperator
Rule.Description: Check that there are no whitespace characters directly after the not (!) operator.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterOpeningBrace
Rule.Description: Check that there is at least one space (blank) or whitespace after each opening brace ("{") for method/class/interface declarations, closure expressions and block statements.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterSemicolon
Rule.Description: Checks that there is at least one space or whitespace following each semicolon separating multiple statements on a single line or the clauses within a classic for loop.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterSwitch
Rule.Description: Check that there is exactly one space (blank) after the switch keyword and before the opening parenthesis.

Rule.name: SpaceAfterWhile
Rule.Description: Check that there is exactly one space (blank) after the while keyword and before the opening parenthesis.

Rule.name: SpaceAroundClosureArrow
Rule.Description: Checks that there is whitespace around the closure arrow (->) symbol

Rule.name: SpaceAroundMapEntryColon
Rule.Description: Check for configured formatting of whitespace around colons for literal Map entries. The characterBeforeColonRegex and characterAfterColonRegex properties specify a regular expression that must match the character before/after the colon.

Rule.name: SpaceAroundOperator
Rule.Description: Check that there is at least one space (blank) or whitespace around each binary operator.

Rule.name: SpaceBeforeClosingBrace
Rule.Description: Check that there is at least one space (blank) or whitespace before each closing brace ("}") for method/class/interface declarations, closure expressions and block statements.

Rule.name: SpaceBeforeCommentDelimiter
Rule.Description: Checks that there is whitespace before comment characters (// and /*)

Rule.name: SpaceBeforeOpeningBrace
Rule.Description: Check that there is at least one space (blank) or whitespace before each opening brace ("{") for method/class/interface declarations, closure expressions and block statements.

Rule.name: SpaceInsideParentheses
Rule.Description: Check for whitespace after opening parentheses and before closing parentheses

Rule.name: SpockIgnoreRestUsed
Rule.Description: If Spock's @IgnoreRest appears on any method, all non-annotated test methods are not executed. This behaviour is almost always unintended. It's fine to use @IgnoreRest locally during development, but when committing code, it should be removed.

Rule.name: SpockMissingAssert
Rule.Description: Spock treats all expressions on the first level of a then or expect block as an implicit assertion. However, everything inside if/for/switch/... blocks is not an implicit 'assert', just a useless comparison (unless wrapped by a 'with' or 'verifyAll'). Please note that the rule might produce false positives, as it relies on method names to determine whether an expression has a boolean type or not.

Rule.name: StatelessClass
Rule.Description: Checks for fields on classes that should remain "stateless" and reentrant. The ignoreFieldNames property (null) specifies one or more field names that should be ignored. The ignoreFieldTypes property specifies one or more field type names that should be ignored. Both can optionally contain wildcard characters ('*' or '?').

Rule.name: StatelessSingleton
Rule.Description: There is no point in creating a stateless Singleton because there is nothing within the class that needs guarding and no side effects to calling the constructor. Just create new instances of the object or write a Utility class with static methods.

Rule.name: StaticCalendarField
Rule.Description: Calendar objects should not be used as static fields. Calendars are inherently unsafe for multihtreaded use. Sharing a single instance across thread boundaries without proper synchronization will result in erratic behavior of the application.

Rule.name: StaticConnection
Rule.Description: Creates violations when a java.sql.Connection object is used as a static field. Database connections stored in static fields will be shared between threads, which is unsafe and can lead to race conditions.

Rule.name: StaticDateFormatField
Rule.Description: DateFormat objects should not be used as static fields. DateFormat are inherently unsafe for multithreaded use. Sharing a single instance across thread boundaries without proper synchronization will result in erratic behavior of the application.

Rule.name: StaticFieldsBeforeInstanceFields
Rule.Description: Enforce that all static fields are above all instance fields within a class

Rule.name: StaticMatcherField
Rule.Description: Matcher objects should not be used as static fields. Matcher instances are inherently unsafe for multithreaded use. Sharing a single instance across thread boundaries without proper synchronization will result in erratic behavior of the application.

Rule.name: StaticMethodsBeforeInstanceMethods
Rule.Description: Enforce that all static methods are above all instance methods within a class

Rule.name: StaticSimpleDateFormatField
Rule.Description: SimpleDateFormat objects should not be used as static fields. SimpleDateFormat are inherently unsafe for multi-threaded use. Sharing a single instance across thread boundaries without proper synchronization will result in erratic behavior of the application.

Rule.name: SwallowThreadDeath
Rule.Description: Checks for code that catches ThreadDeath without re-throwing it.

Rule.name: SynchronizedMethod
Rule.Description: This rule reports uses of the synchronized keyword on methods. Synchronized methods are the same as synchronizing on 'this', which effectively make your synchronization policy public and modifiable by other objects. To avoid possibilities of deadlock, it is better to synchronize on internal objects.

Rule.name: SynchronizedOnBoxedPrimitive
Rule.Description: The code synchronizes on a boxed primitive constant, such as an Integer. Since Integer objects can be cached and shared, this code could be synchronizing on the same object as other, unrelated code, leading to unresponsiveness and possible deadlock

Rule.name: SynchronizedOnGetClass
Rule.Description: Synchronization on getClass rather than class literal. This instance method synchronizes on this.getClass(). If this class is subclassed, subclasses will synchronize on the class object for the subclass, which isn't likely what was intended.

Rule.name: SynchronizedOnReentrantLock
Rule.Description: Synchronizing on a ReentrantLock field is almost never the intended usage. A ReentrantLock should be obtained using the lock() method and released in a finally block using the unlock() method.

Rule.name: SynchronizedOnString
Rule.Description: Synchronization on a String field can lead to deadlock because Strings are interned by the JVM and can be shared.

Rule.name: SynchronizedOnThis
Rule.Description: This rule reports uses of the synchronized blocks where the synchronization reference is 'this'. Doing this effectively makes your synchronization policy public and modifiable by other objects. To avoid possibilities of deadlock, it is better to synchronize on internal objects.

Rule.name: SynchronizedReadObjectMethod
Rule.Description: Catches Serializable classes that define a synchronized readObject method. By definition, an object created by deserialization is only reachable by one thread, and thus there is no need for readObject() to be synchronized. If the readObject() method itself is causing the object to become visible to another thread, that is an example of very dubious coding style.

Rule.name: SystemErrPrint
Rule.Description: Checks for calls to System.err.print(), System.err.println() or System.err.printf().

Rule.name: SystemExit
Rule.Description: Web applications should never call System.exit(). A call to System.exit() is probably part of leftover debug code or code imported from a non-J2EE application.

Rule.name: SystemOutPrint
Rule.Description: Checks for calls to System.out.print(), System.out.println() or System.out.printf().

Rule.name: SystemRunFinalizersOnExit
Rule.Description: Method calls to System.runFinalizersOnExit() should not be allowed. This method is inherently non-thread-safe, may result in data corruption, deadlock, and may effect parts of the program far removed from it's call point. It is deprecated, and it's use strongly discouraged.

Rule.name: TernaryCouldBeElvis
Rule.Description: Checks for ternary expressions where the boolean and true expressions are the same. These can be simplified to an Elvis expression.

Rule.name: ThisReferenceEscapesConstructor
Rule.Description: Reports constructors passing the 'this' reference to other methods. This equals exposing a half-baked objects and can lead to race conditions during initialization. For reference, see 'Java Concurrency Gotchas' by Alex Miller (http://www.slideshare.net/alexmiller/java-concurrency-gotchas-3666977/38) and 'Java theory and practice: Safe construction techniques' by Brian Goetz (http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/java/library/j-jtp0618/index.html).

Rule.name: ThreadLocalNotStaticFinal
Rule.Description: ThreadLocal fields should be static and final. In the most common case a java.lang.ThreadLocal instance associates state with a thread. A non-static non-final java.lang.ThreadLocal field associates state with an instance-thread combination. This is seldom necessary and often a bug which can cause memory leaks and possibly incorrect behavior.

Rule.name: ThreadYield
Rule.Description: Method calls to Thread.yield() should not be allowed. This method has no useful guaranteed semantics, and is often used by inexperienced programmers to mask race conditions.

Rule.name: ThrowError
Rule.Description: Checks for throwing an instance of java.lang.Error.

Rule.name: ThrowException
Rule.Description: Checks for throwing an instance of java.lang.Exception.

Rule.name: ThrowExceptionFromFinallyBlock
Rule.Description: Throwing an exception from a finally block is confusing and can hide the original exception.

Rule.name: ThrowNullPointerException
Rule.Description: Checks for throwing an instance of java.lang.NullPointerException.

Rule.name: ThrowRuntimeException
Rule.Description: Checks for throwing an instance of java.lang.RuntimeException.

Rule.name: ThrowThrowable
Rule.Description: Checks for throwing an instance of java.lang.Throwable.

Rule.name: ToStringReturnsNull
Rule.Description: Checks for toString() methods that return null.

Rule.name: TrailingComma
Rule.Description: Check whether list and map literals contain optional trailing comma.

Rule.name: TrailingWhitespace
Rule.Description: Checks that no lines of source code end with whitespace characters.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryBigDecimalInstantiation
Rule.Description: It is unnecessary to instantiate BigDecimal objects. Instead just use the decimal literal or the 'G' identifier to force the type, such as 123.45 or 123.45G.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryBigIntegerInstantiation
Rule.Description: It is unnecessary to instantiate BigInteger objects. Instead just use the literal with the 'G' identifier to force the type, such as 8G or 42G.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryBooleanExpression
Rule.Description: Checks for unnecessary boolean expressions, including ANDing (&&) or ORing (||) with true, false, null, or a Map/List/String/Number literal. Also checks for negation (!) of true, false, null, or a Map/List/String/Number literal.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryBooleanInstantiation
Rule.Description: Use Boolean.valueOf() for variable values or Boolean.TRUE and Boolean.FALSE for constant values instead of calling the Boolean() constructor directly or calling Boolean.valueOf(true) or Boolean.valueOf(false).

Rule.name: UnnecessaryCallForLastElement
Rule.Description: This rule checks for excessively verbose methods of accessing the last element of an array or list. For instance, it is possible to access the last element of an array by performing array[array.length - 1], in Groovy it is simpler to either call array.last() or array[-1]. The same is true for lists. This violation is triggered whenever a get, getAt, or array-style access is used with an object size check.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryCallToSubstring
Rule.Description: Calling String.substring(0) always returns the original string. This code is meaningless.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryCast
Rule.Description: Checks for unnecessary cast operations

Rule.name: UnnecessaryCatchBlock
Rule.Description: Violations are triggered when a catch block does nothing but throw the original exception. In this scenario there is usually no need for a catch block, just let the exception be thrown from the original code. This condition frequently occurs when catching an exception for debugging purposes but then forgetting to take the catch statement out.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryCollectCall
Rule.Description: Some method calls to Object.collect(Closure) can be replaced with the spread operator. For instance, list.collect { it.multiply(2) } can be replaced by list*.multiply(2). Warning: if a collection is null, collect will return an empty list, while *. will return null.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryCollectionCall
Rule.Description: Useless call to collections. This call doesn't make sense. For any collection c, calling c.containsAll(c) should always be true, and c.retainAll(c) should have no effect.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryConstructor
Rule.Description: This rule detects when a constructor is not necessary; i.e., when there's only one constructor, it's public, has an empty body, and takes no arguments.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryDefInFieldDeclaration
Rule.Description: If a field has a visibility modifier or a type declaration, then the def keyword is unneeded. For instance, 'static def constraints = {}' is redundant and can be simplified to 'static constraints = {}.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryDefInMethodDeclaration
Rule.Description: If a method has a visibility modifier or a type declaration, then the def keyword is unneeded. For instance 'def private method() {}' is redundant and can be simplified to 'private method() {}'.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryDefInVariableDeclaration
Rule.Description: If a variable has a visibility modifier or a type declaration, then the def keyword is unneeded. For instance 'def private n = 2' is redundant and can be simplified to 'private n = 2'.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryDotClass
Rule.Description: To make a reference to a class, it is unnecessary to specify the '.class' identifier. For instance String.class can be shortened to String.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryDoubleInstantiation
Rule.Description: It is unnecessary to instantiate Double objects. Instead just use the double literal or the 'D' identifier to force the type, such as 123.45d or 0.42d.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryElseStatement
Rule.Description: When an if statement block ends with a return statement the else is unnecessary. The logic in the else branch can be run without being in a new scope.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryFail
Rule.Description: In a unit test, catching an exception and immediately calling Assert.fail() is pointless and hides the stack trace. It is better to rethrow the exception or not catch the exception at all.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryFinalOnPrivateMethod
Rule.Description: A private method is marked final. Private methods cannot be overridden, so marking it final is unnecessary.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryFloatInstantiation
Rule.Description: It is unnecessary to instantiate Float objects. Instead just use the float literal with the 'F' identifier to force the type, such as 123.45F or 0.42f.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryGString
Rule.Description: String objects should be created with single quotes, and GString objects created with double quotes. Creating normal String objects with double quotes is confusing to readers.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryGetter
Rule.Description: Checks for explicit calls to getter/accessor methods which can, for the most part, be replaced by property access. A getter is defined as a method call that matches get[A-Z] but not getClass() or get[A-Z][A-Z] such as getURL(). Getters do not take method arguments. The ignoreMethodNames property (null) can specify method names that should be ignored, optionally containing wildcard characters ('*' or '?').

Rule.name: UnnecessaryGroovyImport
Rule.Description: A Groovy file does not need to include an import for classes from java.lang, java.util, java.io, java.net, groovy.lang and groovy.util, as well as the classes java.math.BigDecimal and java.math.BigInteger.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryIfStatement
Rule.Description: Checks for if statements where the if and else blocks (or subsequent fall-through to a return), are merely returning true and false constants. These cases can be replaced by a simple return statement.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryInstanceOfCheck
Rule.Description: This rule finds instanceof checks that cannot possibly evaluate to true. For instance, checking that (!variable instanceof String) will never be true because the result of a not expression is always a boolean.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryInstantiationToGetClass
Rule.Description: Avoid instantiating an object just to call getClass() on it; use the .class public member instead.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryIntegerInstantiation
Rule.Description: It is unnecessary to instantiate Integer objects. Instead just use the literal with the 'I' identifier to force the type, such as 8I or 42i.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryLongInstantiation
Rule.Description: It is unnecessary to instantiate Long objects. Instead just use the literal with the 'L' identifier to force the type, such as 8L or 42L.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryModOne
Rule.Description: Any expression mod 1 (exp % 1) is guaranteed to always return zero. This code is probably an error, and should be either (exp & 1) or (exp % 2).

Rule.name: UnnecessaryNullCheck
Rule.Description: Groovy contains the safe dereference operator, which can be used in boolean conditional statements to safely replace explicit "x == null" tests.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryNullCheckBeforeInstanceOf
Rule.Description: There is no need to check for null before an instanceof; the instanceof keyword returns false when given a null argument.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryObjectReferences
Rule.Description: Violations are triggered when an excessive set of consecutive statements all reference the same variable. This can be made more readable by using a with or identity block.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryOverridingMethod
Rule.Description: The overriding method merely calls the same method defined in a superclass

Rule.name: UnnecessaryPackageReference
Rule.Description: Checks for explicit package reference for classes that Groovy imports by default, such as java.lang.String, java.util.Map and groovy.lang.Closure.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryParenthesesForMethodCallWithClosure
Rule.Description: If a method is called and the only parameter to that method is an inline closure then the parentheses of the method call can be omitted.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryPublicModifier
Rule.Description: The 'public' modifier is not required on methods or classes.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryReturnKeyword
Rule.Description: In Groovy, the return keyword is often optional. If a statement is the last line in a method or closure then you do not need to have the return keyword.

Rule.name: UnnecessarySafeNavigationOperator
Rule.Description: Check for the safe navigation operator (?.) applied to constants and literals, which can never be null.

Rule.name: UnnecessarySelfAssignment
Rule.Description: Method contains a pointless self-assignment to a variable or property.

Rule.name: UnnecessarySemicolon
Rule.Description: Semicolons as line terminators are not required in Groovy: remove them. Do not use a semicolon as a replacement for empty braces on for and while loops; this is a confusing practice.

Rule.name: UnnecessarySetter
Rule.Description: Checks for explicit calls to setter methods which can, for the most part, be replaced by assignment to property. A setter is defined as a method call that matches set[A-Z] but not set[A-Z][A-Z] such as setURL(). Setters take one method argument.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryStringInstantiation
Rule.Description: Use a String literal (e.g., "...") instead of calling the corresponding String constructor (new String("..")) directly.

Rule.name: UnnecessaryTernaryExpression
